newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Leumi can miss Africa Israel deadline.
newsitem.headline: Leumi can miss Africa Israel deadline.

text.p: Bank Leumi can exceed the end-of-year deadline for reducing its holdings in Africa Israel Investments, Israel's Attorney General Michael Ben-Yair ruled.
Under Israeli law, commercial banks must reduce their holdings in non-banking assets to 25 percent by year's end.
Bank Leumi owns 65 percent of Africa Israel, a major holding company with interests in insurance, construction and tourism.

Leumi, Israel's second-largest bank, has reached a preliminary accord for Italian insurer Generali to take control of the insurance holdings, which will be spun off and listed on the bourse. Leumi plans to reduce its holdings in the rest of Africa Israel separately.
This may not be completed by the end of December and Finance Minister Dan Meridor asked Ben-Yair for extra time.

"The attorney general...reached a conclusion that the proposed course of action is in accordance with the purpose of the law and would significantly increase the economic benefit to the state and the Israeli economy," Ben Yair's office said in a statement.
Ben Yair made his ruling after consulations with officials in the Treasury, Bank of Israel and Justice Ministry.

The statement said Ben Yair's ruling took into account the fact that Meridor and the supervisor of banks approve the insurance spin-off. Also, most of the process will have been completed before the deadline, the statement said.
